name: Jami
tagline: Peer-to-peer encrypted communication. No servers, no accounts, full privacy.
shortDescription: Jami (formerly SFLphone) is a peer-to-peer communication platform. Encrypted text, voice, video, file transfer — no central server, no account required. The most private option.
longDescription:
## What it is

Jami (formerly SFLphone) is a peer-to-peer communication platform. All communication is end-to-end encrypted and goes directly between peers (no central server). Text, voice, video, file transfer, screen sharing, conference calls.

## Why we recommend it

If you need the most private communication possible, Jami is the answer. There's no central server, no account, no metadata collection. The trade-off: you need to know the other person's Jami ID (no phone number discovery).

## When to use it

- Maximum privacy communication (no central server)
- File transfer over the same network as the call
- Conferences without paying for a service
- Replacing Signal/Slack for ultra-privacy-conscious teams
installCommand: apt install jami  # or: brew install jami
installInstructions:
**Desktop:** Download from jami.net (Linux, macOS, Windows).
**Mobile:** App Store, Google Play, F-Droid.

No account needed — share your Jami ID with contacts.
pricingDetails: Free. GPL-3.0 licensed. No servers, no fees, no telemetry.
